text:
mara: seeing a cluster-wide bump in local NVMe write iops in eu-west2 since 01:00 UTC, a handful of nodes hit the wear_threshold_critical flag and started early evictions. noticed GPU attach failures for pending jobs. logs: `wear_score` jumped from ~12 to 48 on gnode-187.
devon: omg, just saw a couple of gpu-provision alerts too. is this the nightly scrub + batch window overlap? :thinking_face:
samir: probably. I can see scrub start times aligned with batch launches in the telemetry. scrub cadence got bumped last week for perf reasons.
jen: any quick mitigation we can push? can we throttle janitor on the affected cohorts or delay scrub for hot stripes?
mara: yes, proposing immediate throttle of ephemeral-cleaner on cohort=eu-west2-hot for 30m and revert scrub sampler changes. that should drop sustained writes 40-60%.
ops-bot: deploy plan queued by devops: throttle-janitor-eu-west2 -> patch applied to 7/72 hosts (in progress).
samir: one wrinkle: throttling increases temporary disk footprint, might push more KV cache spills to disk and hurt latency. tradeoff: fewer evictions vs slightly higher tail latency.
devon: what's the cost delta if we keep throttled for 6h vs doing live reshuffle to lower-wear hosts (which might use reserved capacity)?
mara: rough numbers: 6h throttle ~= +$1.2k in egress / extra storage ops; live reshuffle + reserved bursts ~= $3.9k one-off but reduces attach-fail risk. numbers from yesterday's billing window.
jen: given risk of data corruption and rollbacks if evictions continue, I prefer reshuffle if we can do it within the maintenance window. can we hard-drain top 10 wear hosts and move workloads to eu-west2-cold?
samir: we can. I'll run a quick wear-heatmap and produce a drain list. also recommend running `fstrim --verbose` on the cold cohort after move to reclaim free extents and avoid fragmentation. sample command:

```bash
# list candidates
python infra/tools/wear_report.py --region eu-west2 --top 10 --metric wear_score
# drain
kubectl drain gnode-187 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
```
devon: aware of any networking constraints for moving stateful pods across zones? some of these jobs keep a small local cache we can't lose.
mara: we should use `replicate-cache` flag in the rollout to avoid data loss, and fallback to warm-start if replication fails. Ops playbook updated in /playbooks/eviction-handling.md (link).
storage-bot: SMART summary for gnode-187: `SMART health: PASSED`, but `Total_LBAs_Written` increased 2.6x in last 24h. predictive wear threshold estimate: 3.4 weeks at current rate.
jen: yikes. that's the reason for early eviction. ok samir, prioritize the drain list and coordinate with capacity to spin up eu-west2-cold burst nodes.
samir: will do. pushing a 2-step plan in #runbooks: (1) immediate janitor throttle (done), (2) live drain + cold allocate for high-risk hosts, (3) revert scrub sampler tuning and monitor for 2h. I'll post ETA in 10min.
mara: thanks. quick ask: add a temporary alert for `wear_score > 40 && pending_gpu_attach > 0` so we catch this earlier.
devon: I'll add that alert, low-noise channel to eng-oncall and ops-runner.
ops-bot: throttle-janitor-eu-west2 applied to 7/72 hosts (success). next: preparing drain list.
jen: reminder — update cost forecast for the week in the ticket, we’ll need approvals if we hit the reserved-burst plan.
samir: ETA for first drains: 1769871300 (in 3 min). I'll update thread when done.
mara: congrats team. small follow-ups: run filesystem health check post-drain, and schedule a retro to see if scrub cadence change should be rolled back permanently.
storage-bot: post-drain health checks queued. parity checks and inode-scan will run, results posted to this thread.
samir: drains started. moving gnode-187 -> gnode-402 (cold). will confirm when attach cleared.
mara: thanks — marking as incident:investigating. :thumbsup:
